newsitem.title: BURKINA FASO: Burkina Faso says most debt arrears paid off.
newsitem.headline: Burkina Faso says most debt arrears paid off.

text.p: Burkina Faso has paid off the bulk of its debt arrears and is now able to fund investments from the state budget, President Blaise Compaore told state television.

"In 1990 we had debt arrears of 115 billion CFA francs (current value $200 million). By the end of 1995, helped by adjustment measures, we had eliminated all the external debt arrears of 42 billion, and in 1996 we paid off at least 60 billion of the internal debt," he said in an interview late on Thursday.
The West African state, amongst the world's poorest countries, has been following an IMF structural adjustment programme since 1991.
The CFA franc, which it shares with other African states that are part of the Franc Zone, was devalued by 50 percent in 1994, which doubled the size of its external debt.
Campaore said that since 1995 part of government revenue had gone towards investment. Until then, revenue had not even been sufficient to cover government expenditure.
"By being successful with its adjustment, Burkina Faso has, in the eyes of donors, acquired the reputation of a good manager, a serious country," Campaore added.
